[[173 BBY]]''[[Star Wars: The Acolyte: The Visual Guide]]'' establishes that Torbin was 41 [[Standard year|years]] old at the [[time]] of the events of ''[[Star Wars: The Acolyte]]'', which occur in [[132 BBY]] per the reasoning [[Template:TheAcolyteDate|here]]. Therefore, he must have been [[Reproduction|born]] around [[173 BBY]]. It also establishes Torbin was given to the [[Jedi Order]] when he was three years old, equating to around [[170 BBY]]. |death=[[132 BBY]], [[Olega]]The events of ''[[Star Wars: The Acolyte]]'', including Torbin's [[death]] on [[Olega]] in "[[Revenge / Justice]]," take place in [[132 BBY]] per the reasoning [[Template:TheAcolyteDate|here]]. |species=[[Human]]{{Acolyte|Choice}} |gender=[[Gender|Male]] |pronouns=He/him |height=1.8 [[meter]]s (6 [[Foot|ft]]) |mass= |hair=[[Color|Auburn]]{{Acolyte|Revenge / Justice}} |feathers= |eyes=Blue |skin=Light |cyber= |families= |parents=[[Torbin's parents]] |partners= |siblings= |children= |affiliation=*[[Jedi Order]] **[[Brendok four]]{{SW|url=news/the-acolyte-jedi-order|text=How ''The Acolyte'' Challenges How We See Some Members of the Jedi}} |masters=[[Indara]] |apprentices= }} {{Quote|Forgive me. We thought we were doing the right thing.|Torbin, to Mae Aniseya|}} '''Torbin''' was a [[Force-sensitive]] [[human]] [[Gender|male]] from the [[planet]] [[Bonadan]] who served as a [[Jedi]] of the [[Jedi Order]] during the [[High Republic Era]]. Between around [[158 BBY]] and [[157 BBY]], he became the [[Padawan]] of [[Jedi Master]] [[Indara]]. In [[148 BBY]], Torbin and Indara were [[Mission to Brendok|stationed]] on the planet [[Brendok]] along with [[Jedi Knight]] [[Sol]] and Jedi Master [[Kelnacca]]. The Jedi spent seven [[Standard week|weeks]] searching for a [[vergence]] in [[the Force]] on the planet, during which Torbin grew distracted and impatient. During their investigation, the Jedi discovered a [[Brendok coven|coven]] of [[witch]]es lead by [[Mother (title)|Mother]] [[Aniseya]]. Concerned that the witches were training [[Youngling|children]] to [[Force power|use]] the Force, the four Jedi interrupted a [[Rite of Ascension|ceremony]] and requested to test the children they had learned of—the [[Aniseya family|twins]] [[Verosha Aniseya|Verosha "Osha"]] and [[Mae-ho Aniseya|Mae-ho "Mae" Aniseya]]—to see if they were Force-sensitive. Aniseya initially refused and used the Force to incapacitate Torbin while threatening the other Jedi, but reluctantly agreed after being persuaded by Osha and Indara. The next [[Local day|day]], Torbin took [[blood]] tests from the [[twin]]s as part of their testing. The results of the tests showed an irregularity, which the Jedi believed could be a sign of the vergence they were searching for. Thinking that proof of the vergence would allow them to return home, Torbin took a [[Jedi outland speeder bike|speeder bike]] to the witches' [[Brendok fortress|fortress]] and was pursued by the rest of the group, who sought to prevent him from starting a conflict. However, when Sol caught up with Torbin, the two worked together to enter the fortress to save the twins, believing them to be in danger. In the fortress, a skirmish broke out after Sol mistakenly believed Aniseya to be using [[Dark side of the Force|dark]] [[magick]]s and [[Death|killed]] her. When Kelnacca arrived at the fortress, he was [[Possession|possessed]] by the witches and attacked Torbin and Sol. During their fight, Torbin lost his left [[eye]] after being slammed into a wall by Kelnacca. Indara then arrived and freed Kelnacca from the spell, inadvertently killing the witches in the process. Sol tried to rescue Osha and Mae from a [[fire]] that had broken out, but only succeeded in saving Osha, with Mae being presumed dead. Around a [[147 BBY|year later]], Torbin completed his [[Jedi training]], attaining the rank of Jedi Knight. Around [[142 BBY]], after becoming a Jedi Master, Torbin took the [[Barash Vow]] and entered a silent state of [[meditation]] to atone for his role in the incident on Brendok. In [[132 BBY]], Mae began [[Mae's quest|targeting]] the four Jedi who had been stationed there, both to seek revenge and please her [[The Stranger|master]]. After [[Indara's murder|killing]] Indara, Mae tracked Torbin to the [[Olega Jedi temple|Jedi temple]] on the planet [[Olega]], where her first attempt to kill Torbin failed due to a [[Force barrier]] he manifested though the Barash Vow. She later returned with [[bunta]] [[poison]] and offered Torbin the choice to either confess his crimes to the [[Jedi High Council|Jedi Council]] or drink the poison to receive forgiveness. At this, Torbin finally broke his silence and willingly drank the poison, killing himself. Following Torbin's death, the Jedi, including Sol, continued their investigation into Mae's murders. Sol was [[Duel on Brendok|killed]] by Osha when she sided with Mae's master, after which Jedi Master [[Vernestra Rwoh]] covered up the murders, insisting that Sol had been responsible for the killings of Torbin and the other Jedi who had been stationed on Brendok. ==Biography== ===The Brendok incident=== ====Searching for a vergence==== {{Quote|…I want to go home to Coruscant.''"
"''I know, But we're on a mission.''"
"''We've been here for seven weeks. And there's no one here, and if we were going to find something, we probably would've found it by now.''"
"''A hundred years ago, this planet was catalogued as lifeless because of a hyperspace disaster. Yet this planet, Brendok, is thriving.|Torbin and Indara|audio=IndaraTorbinMissionTalk-Choice.flac|}} [[File:TorbinBoredOnBrendok-Choice.png|thumb|right|300px|Torbin used a device to analyze samples while assisting in the investigation.]] Torbin was a [[Force-sensitive]] [[human]] [[Gender|male]] [[Homeworld|from]] the [[planet]] [[Bonadan]] who was [[Reproduction|born]] around [[173 BBY]] during the [[High Republic Era]]. Around [[170 BBY]], a [[Unidentified Jedi seeker (Torbin)|Jedi seeker]] identified Torbin as having [[The Force|Force]] potential, after which his impoverished [[Torbin's parents|parents]] gave him to the [[Jedi Order]]. Between around [[158 BBY]] and [[157 BBY]],The events of ''[[Star Wars: The Acolyte]]'' take place in [[132 BBY]] per the reasoning [[:Template:TheAcolyteDate|here]]. ''[[Star Wars: The Acolyte: The Visual Guide]]'' specifies that Torbin began [[Jedi training|training]] under [[Indara]] when the former was sixteen [[Standard year|years]] old and the latter was twenty-eight years old. As ''The Visual Guide'' specifies their [[death]]s—which took place during ''The Acolyte''—occurred at ages forty-one and fifty-four, respectively, Torbin must have commenced his training between around [[158 BBY]] and [[157 BBY]]. Torbin became the [[Padawan]] of [[Jedi Master]] [[Indara]]. On occasion, Torbin ventured into the raucous lower levels of the planet [[Coruscant]] alone. At one point, he reforged his [[Torbin's lightsaber|lightsaber]] with a newly gathered [[kyber crystal]], which bonded to form a [[Color|yellow]] blade. In [[148 BBY]],{{TheAcolyteDate}} "[[Revenge / Justice]]" establishes that Torbin was stationed on [[Brendok]] sixteen [[Standard year|years]] before its events, equating to [[148 BBY]]. Torbin was [[Mission to Brendok|stationed]] on the planet [[Brendok]] along with Indara, [[Jedi Knight]] [[Sol]], and Jedi Master [[Kelnacca]]. The group became known as the [[Brendok four]]. On Brendok, the Jedi investigated the life present on the planet, as it was thriving despite being catalogued as lifeless after the [[Great Hyperspace Disaster]] of [[232 BBY]].''[[Star Wars: The High Republic Character Encyclopedia]]'' Torbin assisted with the investigation by placing samples into an analyzing device. Seven [[Standard week|weeks]] into the mission, the Jedi sat around a campfire and [[Diet|ate]] [[nuna]] [[Limb|legs]] Kelnacca had cooked for the group. However, Torbin did not eat them, and when Indara told him he needed to, he claimed not to be hungry. Indara warned him not to insult a Wookiee's cooking, to which Torbin responded by complaining that he already eaten nuna legs often during the mission and wanted to return home to Coruscant. [[File:TorbinWantsToGoHome-Choice.png|thumb|300px|left|Torbin expressed his desire to return to Coruscant to the team.]] As the Jedi ate, Torbin further complained that he did not understand the importance or purpose of their mission. Indara told him to calm himself, and she and Sol explained that they were looking for a [[vergence]], a concentration of Force energy centered around a location. The next [[Standard day|day]], as the Jedi continued their investigation, Torbin collected more samples to be analyzed. Indara and Sol watched Torbin and discussed his feelings about the mission. Indara noted that he was distracted, and Sol said he was disturbed and unbalanced, to which Indara replied that Sol was confusing Torbin's feelings with his own. She further added that rather than giving Torbin answers to ease his mind, she taught him to seek answers for himself. Indara then instructed Sol to split up from the group as they continued their search. ====Investigating the witches==== {{Quote|If you want your Padawan returned to his right mind, I suggest you all leave. Now.|Mother Aniseya, threatening the Jedi|}} [[File:JediOnBrendok-Destiny.png|thumb|right|300px|Torbin and the other Jedi in the witches' fortress]] After splitting up, Sol found the [[Aniseya family|twins]] [[Verosha Aniseya|Verosha "Osha"]] and [[Mae-ho Aniseya|Mae-ho "Mae" Aniseya]] and followed them back to a [[Brendok fortress|fortress]]. There, he learned of a [[Brendok coven|coven]] of [[witch]]es led by [[Mother (title)|Mother]] [[Aniseya]] and became concerned they were training [[Youngling|children]] to use the Force, known to the witches as the Thread. After Sol reported this to the other Jedi, Torbin suggested the witches could be [[Nightsisters]], but Indara disagreed. Indara wanted to ask the [[Jedi High Council|Jedi Council]] for guidance, but Sol persuaded her to allow him to show them what he had seen, and the four Jedi rode [[Jedi outland speeder bike|speeder bikes]] to the [[fortress]]. After they arrived outside, Kelnacca [[Slicer|sliced]] the controls to enter the fortress, and Indara stated she would go in alone. However, Torbin insisted they escort her, and Sol convinced her that they should stay as a group. The Jedi entered the [[Rite of Ascension courtyard|courtyard]] where the twins' [[Rite of Ascension]] ceremony, in which they would become witches, was being held. Indara introduced the four Jed and stated their concerns about the witches training children against [[Galactic Republic]] law. The witches refuted Indara's claims, stating that Brendok was not part of the Republic and that they had no children.{{Acolyte|Destiny (The Acolyte)}} As they spoke, Aniseya used a [[Force power|Thread ability]] to make Torbin experience a [[Force vision|vision]] of himself alone with her in the courtyard. She praised Torbin, then spoke to him about his desires and told him to ask her for help escaping Brendok. Eventually, Torbin took a deep breath and admitted he wanted to return to Coruscant. [[File:AniseyaInTorbinsHead-Choice.png|thumb|left|300px|Aniseya was able to invade and take control of Torbin's mind.]] At the same time, Kelnacca noticed the [[twin]]s, and Indara asked them to come out of the crowd. When Sol suggested that Osha be tested to [[Jedi training|train]] as a Jedi, she asked Aniseya—her [[Parent|mother]]—for permission. In Torbin's vision, Aniseya ordered him to kneel, and he complied. The other Jedi turned to see Torbin's real body also kneel as his [[eye]]s turned black and he began gasping. Aniseya threatened the Jedi, telling them she would not return Torbin to his right mind unless they left. However, Osha and Indara continued to persuade her, and she reluctantly agreed to allow her children to be tested and released Torbin. Following this, the Jedi exited the courtyard and returned to their [[Polan-717 Jedi transport|Polan shuttle]], designated [[Polan GX-8|GX-8]].[[Star Wars Encyclopedia of Starfighters and Other Vehicles (second edition)|''Star Wars Encyclopedia of Starfighters and Other Vehicles'', second edition]] ====Testing the twins==== {{Quote|Do all Jedis get one of those?''"
"''After much training, yes.|Osha and Torbin, discussing lightsabers|}} [[File:TorbinMaeBloodSample-Choice.png|thumb|right|300px|Torbin took a blood sample from Mae before she was tested.]] The next day, Osha and Mae arrived at the site of the Jedi's encampment to be tested. While Mae tried to persuade Osha to fail the test on purpose, Torbin spoke with their other mother, [[Koril]]. Before Mae was tested, Torbin took a [[blood]] sample from her after first assuring the girl he would not hurt her. Torbin was then present while Sol and Indara administered her test, which she deliberately failed. After Mae completed her testing, she exited the Jedi's [[shuttle]], followed by Torbin, who informed Osha they were ready for her. Aboard the [[Starship|ship]], Torbin took a blood sample from Osha as well. When she asked him if all Jedi got a [[lightsaber]], he told her they did, but only after much training. Torbin remained present while Sol and Indara tested Osha, who attempted to fail the test at first, but was persuaded to admit that she did wish to become a Jedi. After, Indara told Torbin to test the girls' blood samples. That night, Indara informed the group that the Jedi Council would not permit them to bring the twins to Coruscant, and Torbin expressed his opinion that the witches were dangerous. Torbin also asked if they would be allowed to return home, and was disappointed when Indara told him they would not be. Sol argued against the Council's decision to Indara and was eventually interrupted when the blood tests were completed. Torbin checked the test results and realized that the girls' symbiotes were the same, an impossible result even for identical twins. When Sol suggested that a vergence could be the cause, Torbin—though he was frightened by the development like his fellow Jedi{{InsiderCite|231|A Certain Point of View}}—became excited, convinced that the twins were the proof they needed of a vergence. Thinking that the children were thus his way home, he took a [[speeder bike]] and rode toward the fortress, ignoring Sol's warning to stop. Indara ordered Sol to stop him, and he pursued Torbin on another speeder bike while Indara and Kelnacca followed in the Polan. ====Battle in the fortress==== {{Quote|You should not have brought him here.''"
"''No. My mind is fortified!''"
"''Not you.|Koril and Torbin|}} [[File:TorbinVsKoril-Choice.png|thumb|left|350px|Torbin and Koril prepare to face each other]] Outside the fortress, Sol caught up with Torbin, who informed him that he believed the twins were locked inside, adding that the [[Turbolift|elevator]] was not functioning. Despite Sol's orders from Indara to stop Torbin, he instead worked with the Padawan to enter the fortress. Sol told Torbin not to let the witches inside his head again and asked him to help save the girls. Torbin agreed and the two began climbing the fortress wall. Meanwhile, Indara, unable to land the ship, asked Kelnacca to jump and stop Torbin before he started a conflict. Inside the fortress, Sol and Torbin confronted the witches, with Sol asking about the twins' creation. Noticing many of the witches aiming drawn [[bow]]s at them, Torbin drew his lightsaber, but Sol calmed him before he ignited it. Mae entered the courtyard to warn Aniseya about a [[fire]] she had started, but Koril misinterpreted her cry for help and, in a desperate move, began to attack Torbin,{{DarthVaderCite|70|The Dark Side}} who ignited his blade. To ensure no one would be injured, Aniseya turned herself and Mae into a black mist, but Sol mistakenly believed her to be using [[Dark side of the Force|dark]] [[magick]]s and [[Death|fatally]] stabbed her. After Aniseya died, Koril ordered Mae to run, and she began fighting with Sol. While they fought, Torbin used his lightsaber to deflect attacks from the witches, who had begun firing their bows. As parts of the fortress began to collapse due the fire set by Mae, Sol yelled to Torbin that the twins were trapped inside. Koril disappeared by turning to black mist, and Torbin felt the effect's of the witches' power again. Koril told the Jedi that they should not have brought "him" there, and Torbin responded that his mind was fortified. Koril clarified she was not referring to Torbin, and Kelnacca arrived while being [[Possession|possessed]] by the witches. The [[Wookiee]] ignited his [[Kelnacca's lightsaber|lightsaber]] and engaged Torbin and Sol in a [[lightsaber duel]]. He was able to overpower them, then [[Force push|pushed]] them both back with the Force. Torbin evaded more strikes from Kelnacca while crawling backward away from him, but the Wookiee picked him up and slammed him into a wall, costing him his left eye. [[File:KelnaccaCrushesTorbin-Choice.png|thumb|right|300px|Torbin is pinned against a wall by Kelnacca]] Torbin managed to block a strike from Kelnacca as he was held against the wall, and Sol freed Torbin from Kelnacca's grip. The Padawan collapsed to the ground while Sol continued [[Lightsaber combat|dueling]] Kelnacca, eventually disarming him and fighting him in [[Unarmed combat|hand-to-hand combat]]. As Kelnacca attempted to strangle Sol, Indara arrived, freeing him from the witches' [[Magic|spell]] and unintentionally killing the witches in the process.{{WebCite|url=https://nerdist.com/article/the-acolyte-showrunner-leslye-headland-interview|text=THE ACOLYTE's Leslye Headland on Episode 7, Witches, Vergences, Qui-Gon, and Anakin – Nerdist|author=[https://nerdist.com/author/michael-walsh Michael Walsh]|date=2024-07-10|work=[[Wikipedia:Nerdist|Nerdist]]|archivedate=20240917200152}} Indara then ordered Sol to rescue the twins from the fire, but he was only able to save Osha, with Mae being presumed dead. Later, the Jedi traveled back to Coruscant aboard their ship, and Indara harshly scolded Torbin and Sol for their actions. Indara got into an altercation with Sol when he tried to walk away, and Torbin called out to his master, who stopped. Torbin asked what they would tell the Council, and Indara responded they would claim the deaths of the coven members were caused by the fire started by Mae. Osha later became Sol's Padawan, but ultimately left the Order. ===Finding absolution=== ====The Barash Vow==== {{Quote|Master Torbin. We have unfinished business. Attack me with all your strength.|Mae Aniseya, to Torbin|}} [[File:TorbinLevitation-RevengeJustice.png|thumb|left|250px|Torbin meditating during his Barash Vow]] Around [[147 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: The Acolyte: The Visual Guide]]'' establishes that Torbin was forty-one [[Standard year|years]] old at the [[time]] of the events of ''[[Star Wars: The Acolyte]]'', which occur in [[132 BBY]] per the reasoning [[Template:TheAcolyteDate|here]]. It also establishes Torbin was twenty-six years old when he passed his [[Jedi Trials]], equating to around [[147 BBY]], and that he was thirty-one when he became a [[Jedi Master]], equating to around [[142 BBY]]. Torbin passed his [[Jedi Trials]] and became a Jedi Knight. Around [[142 BBY]], Torbin attained the rank of Jedi Master after years of studious devotion. He then traveled to the planet [[Olega]], where he relinquished his lightsaber to the stewards of Olega's [[Olega Jedi temple|Jedi temple]] and took the [[Barash Vow]] to repent for his role in the incident on Brendok. As part of his vow, Torbin did not speak and entered a trance-like [[Levitation|levitating]] [[meditation]]. Jedi Master [[Cord Taunus]] monitored Torbin as part of his duties as the Steward of Olega. During his vow, Torbin meditated on his past failures and intended to lose his conscious self in the currents of the Force. Although he outwardly appeared tranquil while meditating, he exuded a turbulence in the Force that manifested as a [[Force barrier|barrier]]. In [[132 BBY]], ten years after Torbin took the Barash Vow, Mae began [[Mae's quest|targeting]] the four Jedi who had been stationed on Brendok, both to seek revenge and to please her master, a [[Sith]] known as [[the Stranger]]. In addition to killing the four Jedi, Mae's master also tasked her with defeating one of them without a [[weapon]]. After [[Indara's murder|killing]] Indara, Mae found Torbin in the [[Jedi temple]] on Olega, where he was still in his levitating state. There, Mae challenged him to attack her, but he remained silent. Mae then attempted to attack Torbin, but he continued to remain unresponsive while his barrier deflected her attacks, and she was forced to flee when her break-in was noticed by other Jedi. After learning of the intrusion, Jedi Master [[Vernestra Rwoh]] asked Sol to investigate and bring Osha, who had been a suspect in Indara's murder, with him to Olega. Upon hearing their destination, Osha noted Torbin was there. ====Final atonement==== {{Quote|I've been waiting for you, Mae.|Torbin, to Mae Aniseya|}} The next day, Mae visited the [[Olega Apothecary]] and informed her accomplice, Qimir—who was also secretly her [[Sith Master]]—of the difficulty she had had with attacking Torbin. Qimir advised her to find his weakness, but she insisted Torbin lacked one and requested Qimir make her a [[poison]]. He agreed, but warned Mae that her next target, Kelnacca, would be even more difficult to defeat without a weapon. Qimir further advised Mae that Torbin was not as serene or impenetrable as she believed, as he had not actually found peace and instead needed absolution. [[File:TorbinSuicide-RevengeJustice.png|thumb|right|300px|Torbin killed himself to atone for his actions on Brendok.]] Mae returned to Torbin's quarters with the poison at the same time Sol's team arrived outside the Olega temple. While Taunus told Sol about the previous night's events, Mae spoke to Torbin, asking if he remembered her and telling him she knew he had taken the Barash Vow in search of peace. Outside the temple, Sol asked to speak with Torbin. Although Taunus informed Sol of Torbin's silence, Sol believed he would still be willing to speak to him, and the Jedi Master took Sol's team to Torbin's quarters. As they walked through the temple, Mae placed the poison in front of Torbin and offered him a choice to either confess his crime to the Jedi Council or to drink the poison and receive forgiveness. He finally responded to this, lowering himself to the ground and telling Mae he had been waiting for her. After a final request for forgiveness, Torbin ingested the poison, killing himself. Osha, who had separated from the rest of Sol's team, arrived in Torbin's quarters ahead of them and found his body. She picked up the empty poison vial and smelled it, then closed Torbin's eyes. When the Jedi entered the room, they were initially suspicious of Osha, but Jedi Knight [[Yord Fandar]] confirmed her innocence. The Jedi inspected Torbin's body, and when Sol realized that Torbin had taken the poison willingly, Osha identified the poison as [[bunta]] from Brendok. Using that information, the Jedi found Qimir and learned from him that Mae was targeting the four Jedi who had been on Brendok. Sol [[Skirmish on Olega|confronted]] Mae that night and accused her of killing Indara and Torbin, but she was able to escape from the Jedi. ====Legacy==== {{Quote|You're under arrest for the murder of Master Indara, the murder of—the murder of Master Torbin, the murder of Master Kelnacca, and the fire that killed your family.|Jecki Lon, while attempting to arrest Mae Aniseya|{{Acolyte|Night}} }} [[File:VernestraSenateTribunal-TheAcolyte.png|thumb|left|300px|Vernestra Rwoh claimed to a Senate committee that Torbin and his fellow Jedi had been killed by Sol.]] In the [[Imperial Palace|Jedi Temple]] on Coruscant, Vernestra Rwoh convened a small council to discuss Mae and her targets. During the meeting, [[hologram]]s of Torbin, Kelnacca, and Indara were shown. The holograms of Torbin and Indara, who had already been killed, turned red. At the conclusion of the meeting, Rwoh sent a team to [[Mission to Khofar|travel]] to{{Acolyte|Day (episode)}} the planet [[Khofar]] to extract Kelnacca from his post there. On Kohfar, Qimir and Mae discussed her failure to kill Torbin and Indara without a weapon, with Mae arguing that she had succeeded in killing her targets. During the Jedi mission, Sol's Padawan, [[Jecki Lon]], encountered Mae and attempted to arrest her for the murders of Torbin and Indara, as well as Kelnacca, who had been killed by Mae's master, but she was unsuccessful. Sol was later [[Duel on Brendok|killed]] by Osha on Brendok after she chose to side with Mae's master. After, Rwoh claimed to a committee of [[senator]]s that the Jedi sent to Brendok, including Torbin, had started a conflict with the witches that resulted in many casualties and had conspired to cover it up.{{Acolyte|The Acolyte (episode)}} She then lied that Sol had been behind the murders of the Jedi to maintain the cover story when the truth threatened to come out. Rwoh told the senators that Sol was now dead after presumably taking his own life and assured them than an external review of the Order was not necessary. ==Personality and traits== {{Quote|Calm yourself, Padawan. Do not center on your anxieties.|Indara, to Torbin|}} [[File:Torbin-AcolyteVG.png|thumb|right|200px|Torbin with his lightsaber]] Torbin was a human male with auburn [[hair]] and a beard. He had light skin and blue eyes, and stood 1.8 [[meter]]s, or six feet, tall. He had a youthful visage prior to receiving scars over his left eye on Brendok and undergoing psychological trauma. In his youth, Torbin was a headstrong student. Working in the field frustrated him, and he longed to return to the serenity of Coruscant.{{Databank|torbin|Torbin}} As a Padawan, Torbin possessed an impulse to stay ever-mobile. He had a drive to make a difference, wanting to do something meaningful and impactful, and disliked routine. On Brendok, Torbin was distracted and impatient, disobeying Indara when he thought he had found a way to return to Coruscant. Sol believed he was disturbed and unbalanced. Torbin was put on edge by the unanswered questions about Brendok's vivid biosphere, and the seven weeks of scouting and analysis gnawed away at his patience. Later, he took the Barash Vow in a vain search for self-forgiveness. Torbin's particular manifestation of the vow was sculpted by his encounter on Brendok. ==Powers and abilities== Torbin was Force-sensitive and capable of levitating for an extended period of [[time]] while simultaneously projecting a Force barrier. The impenetrable shield he errected was a unique side effect of his Barash Vow and was involuntarily projected to protect him while he searched for self-forgiveness. As a Padawan, Torbin handled his lightsaber in a defensive style that emphasized an ever-moving blade that carved wide arcs around him for protection. As he aged, his approach became more tempered with precision. ==Equipment== Torbin wielded a yellow-bladed lightsaber, which he reforged prior to the Brendok mission and later relinquished before taking the Barash Vow. He used a device to analyze samples while assisting in the search for a vergence on Brendok. As a Padawan, Torbin's [[Jedi apparel]] consisted of a brown sleeveless linen wrap worn under a gold tunic and a brown heavy weave long-sleeved [[robe]] with a pleated neckline. He also wore brown [[boot]]s and a [[utility belt]] with stowage pockets in which he stored recon tools and nutrient concentrate cylinders. During the time Torbin spent taking the Barash Vow, he wore white and gold [[temple robes]]. They became faded after wearing them for a [[Standard decade|decade]], and they had a featureless obi [[sash]] that lacked a utility [[belt]], as he had no need for one. ==Behind the scenes== ===Development=== {{Quote|Torbin is definitely suffering from a relatable blind spot. Just any person that's ever been an eighteen-year-old who's on a camping trip they don't want to be on, like just you know is struggling with 'if I don't see the endpoint then how am I supposed to be patient?'|Leslye Headland|{{YouTube|video=QlGqaQG1F2M|text=Leslye Headland Answers our Acolyte Questions and Teases for the Finale!|name=Star Wars Explained|date=2024-7-15}}}} [[File:EarlyTorbinConcept-ArtOfAcolyte.png|thumb|right|250px|Early concept art by Calum Alexander Watt]] Torbin first appeared in "[[Revenge / Justice]]," the second episode of the live-action [[Disney+]] series ''[[Star Wars: The Acolyte]]'', which aired on [[June 4]], 2024.{{SW|url=news/the-acolyte-teaser-poster|text=''The Acolyte'' Teaser Poster, Premiere Date Revealed}} The character was first depicted in a trailer shown exclusively at [[Celebration Europe (2023)|Celebration Europe]]{{CelebrationTrailer|''[[Star Wars: The Acolyte]]''|Celebration Europe (2023)}} on [[April 7]], [[2023]],{{SW|url=news/swce-2023-lucasfilm-studio-showcase|text=SWCE 2023: 11 Highlights from Lucasfilm's Studio Showcase}} and he was identified in his [[Databank (2014-)|databank]] entry on [[March 19]], 2024.{{SW|url=news/the-acolyte-trailer|text=Darkness Rises in ''The Acolyte'' Final Trailer and Key Art}} Torbin was portrayed by [[Dean-Charles Chapman]]. [[Luke Scott]] and [[Christopher Tomkins]] were his stunt doubles. Showrunner [[Leslye Headland]] said that the Jedi on Brendok were operating from a blind spot, with Torbin's blind spot being relatable and the cause of his impatience. Headland compared Torbin to an eighteen-year-old who was on a camping trip that they did not want to be on and did not understand the point of. She also said Torbin took the events on Brendok particularly hard, and that like Osha and Mae, Torbin suffered from the "worst kind of guilt" caused by mistakes made at a young age, which would be difficult to make amends for. Headland believed that Torbin never made peace with the mistakes he made and that he was in a trapped state of mind, which she thought went thematically well with Torbin being literally trapped in his mind by Aniseya. For the show's original characters,{{OfficialYouTube|channel=@RottenTomatoesTV|name=Rotten Tomatoes|link=Wikipedia:Rotten Tomatoes|video=hkJos35CuV0|text='The Acolyte' Cast on New Lightsabers and Droids|date=2024-05-30}} including Torbin, Headland personally selected the color of their lightsabers based on the aesthetics of the scene they appeared in and the character's personality. According to VFX supervisor [[Julian Foddy]], having a shimmering bubble around Torbin was considered but was ultimately not shown, as the Force is traditionally invisible and it was determined that rippling would feel too magical.''[[The Art of Star Wars: The Acolyte]]'' [[Joshua Polley]]'s prop department and [[James McKeown]]'s prop manufacturing team created lightsabers with lucite hilts and embedded LED lights for characters in ''The Acolyte'', including Torbin. [[Calum Alexander Watt]] created early concept art of Torbin, and [[Barbra Araujo]] created costume concept art for him.''[[The Art of Star Wars: The Acolyte]]'' Concept art of Torbin being attacked and being found dead was created by [[Adam Brockbank]] under supervision by production designer [[Kevin Jenkins]].{{Instagram|username=brockbankadam|url=brockbankadam/p/C-pwTG4KfRF|name=[[Adam Brockbank]]|date=2024-08-14|quote=Torbin found dead The Acolyte Production designer Kevin Jenkins|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/wip/8exUF|archivefile=File:TorbinsQuartersConcept.jpg}}{{Instagram|username=brockbankadam|url=brockbankadam/p/DAVnP8hMTDW|name=[[Adam Brockbank]]|date=2024-09-25|quote=Torbin’s quarters the Acolyte Production designer Kevin Jenkins|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/wip/M2O9l|archivefile=File:AdamBrockbank-TorbinsQuartersPost.png}} Brockbank also created concept art of Torbin levitating in his quarters. [[Vincent Jenkins]] created three pieces of concept art of Torbin and the other Jedi sitting together for the Brendok campfire scene.{{Instagram|username=vincentjenkinsjnr|url=p/C_BPeG1IH7N|name=[[Vincent Jenkins]]|date=2024-08-23|quote=Concept for Star Wars "The Acolyte" #starwars #conceptart #theacolyte #art|archiveurl=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/v7MWd|archivefile=File:VincentJenkins-BrendokJediFireside1post.png}} {{Instagram|username=vincentjenkinsjnr|url=p/C_IVODEiq5w|name=[[Vincent Jenkins]]|date=2024-08-26|quote=The Acolyte. Concept art #starwars #theacolyte #conceptart #painting #illustration|archiveurl=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/Hqf23|archivefile=File:VincentJenkins-BrendokJediFireside2post.png}} [[Stephen Tappin]] created concept art of the Jedi in the Brendok courtyard. ===Concept art gallery=== {{Gallery |source=''[[Star Wars: The Acolyte]]'' |storyboards= |concept= File:EarlyTorbinConcept-ArtOfAcolyte.png|Early concept art, Calum Alexander Watt File:TorbinCostumeConcept-ArtOfAcolyte.png|Costume concept, Barbra Araujo File:TorbinFoundDeadConcept.jpg|Torbin found dead, Adam Brockbank under supervision by Kevin Jenkins File:TorbinsQuartersConcept.jpg|Intruder at the Olega temple, Adam Brockbank under supervision by Kevin Jenkins File:TorbinsQuartersConcept-ArtOfAcolyte.png|Torbin's quarters, Adam Brockbank File:BrendokJediFireside-VincentJenkins.jpg|Concept art of the Brendok Jedi by a campfire, Vincent Jenkins File:BrendokJediFireside2-VincentJenkins.jpg|Concept art of the Brendok Jedi by a campfire, Vincent Jenkins File:BrendokJediFireside3-ArtOfAcolyte.png|Concept art of the Brendok Jedi by a campfire, Vincent Jenkins File:BrendokCourtyardSlaughter-ArtOfAcolyte.png|Brendok courtyard slaughter, Stephen Tappin |digital= |in-progress= }} ===Filming=== {{Quote|We rehearsed the fight for weeks, and I loved working with JJ and Dean.|Joonas Suotamono on Kelnacca's fight against Torbin and Sol|{{InsiderCite|230|Kelnacca Kaos}} }} [[File:Dean-CharlesChapman.jpg|thumb|left|225px|Torbin was portrayed by Dean-Charles Chapman.]] Kelnacca actor [[Joonas Suotamo]] worked closely with Chapman and [[Lee Jung-jae]], who portrayed Sol, while training for their fight scene in the Brendok fortress. The fight was rehearsed for several weeks, and Suotamo said he loved working with Chapman and Jung-jae. During the shot where Kelnacca tossed Torbin and pinned him to a wall, wires were used, as Suotamo could not lift Chapman with one hand. Most of the shots in the fight involved the actors, but their stunt doubles were used for some scenes, such as those with difficult wire setups. The scene was filmed in a warehouse at Arborfield Film Studios, an old military base in the [[Wikipedia:United Kingdom|United Kingdom]]. The campfire scene on Brendok was shot at [[Pinewood Studios]]{{Lucasfilm|url=news/lucasfilm-on-location-the-acolyte|text=Lucasfilm on Location: ''The Acolyte''}} in the United Kingdom{{WebCite|url=https://www.fanthatracks.com/news/the-acolyte-a-journey-to-the-filming-locations-part-2-uk|text=The Acolyte: A journey to the filming locations Part 2: UK|archivedate=20250304030611}} from [[December 8]] to [[December 10|10]], 2022. Other scenes on Brendok were shot in [[Wikipedia:Wales|Wales]]. The entrance to the Brendok fortress was shot at Upper Neuadd Reservoir and Dam in Wales, and interior shots were filmed at [[Shinfield Studios]], [[Wikipedia:England|England]].{{Lucasfilm|url=news/julian-foddy-acolyte|text=''The Acolyte'' Visual Effects Supervisor Julian Foddy}} Interior shots of the Jedi's transport ship were also shot at Shinfield Studios.{{WebCite|url=https://www.fanthatracks.com/news/the-acolyte-a-journey-to-the-filming-locations-part-1-madeira|text=The Acolyte: A journey to the filming locations Part 1: Madeira|archivedate=20241204220147}} The site of the Jedi ship{{WebCite|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cx92exjz98ro|text=Star Wars show swaps galaxy far, far away for Wales|archivedate=20240714093614}} and the locations where the Jedi explored and catalogued Brendok were filmed at Upper Neuadd Reservoir.
